newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Moroccan moves towards phone liberalisation.
newsitem.headline: Moroccan moves towards phone liberalisation.

text.p: A Moroccan parliamentary commission is examining plans to liberalise the state telecommunications network which Prime Minister Abdellatif Filali said would attract private investment and employ modern technology.
The official news agency MAP said on Tuesday that Filali told the commission that the state would continue to oversee the network through an agency set up by his office.

Filali said splitting the existing telecommunications and postal services into two enterprises, respectively called Ittissalat al-Maghrib (Moroccan communications) and Barid al-Maghrib (Moroccan post), would meet two demands.
These were to move with technological progress and to coordinate with Spanish foreign partners within an integrated world economic order, he said.

The prime minister, addressing the commission on Monday, said Morocco needed to develop strategic relations with specialised international companies in order to bring Moroccan telecommunications to international standard, and ensure the transfer of technology and expertise.
Liberalisation of telecommunications should attract investment and create a climate of competitiveness which would lead to lower tariffs and improved services, MAP reported him as saying.
He told the commission that liberalisation of communications should create job opportunities.
MAP said the commission would soon resume its debate on the liberalisation law before it goes to the 333-seat majority centre-right parliament.
